headline: High-risk data leakage and cascading-error pathways exist because B reads/writes files and APIs while A is a document processor with no isolation or provenance controls.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A has no filesystem, clipboard, MCP, or stdin/stdout surfaces, so it cannot directly inject B through a shared channel. B does read files and process API inputs, but the pair lacks a documented bridge from A to B. The only plausible pathway is unusual manual copy/paste or external file transfer, so blast radius is small.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies A's output into B's prompt or files, prompt injection becomes possible.
IF a shared filesystem or message queue is introduced between the agents, B may ingest attacker-controlled content.
mitigations: Keep A and B on separate workspaces.
Disable manual copy/paste between agent outputs and B inputs during runs.
Add a short human review step before B consumes any A-generated text.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all A outputs before B reads them.

B_data_leakage.rationale: B touches configuration secrets and can read/write local files and call APIs by default, while A is a document-processing agent with no filesystem access or network egress. The pairwise risk is that B may expose sensitive course data or secrets if A-produced documents are placed into B's workspace. This is not provably blocked, and mitigations are not enabled by default.
conditions: IF A-generated documents containing secrets are placed in B's local workspace, B can read them.
IF B sends retrieved file contents through its allowlisted network APIs, those contents may leave the local environment.
mitigations: Store secrets outside any shared workspace.
Restrict B to a redacted input directory.
Rotate any exposed API keys after test runs.
Review B's outbound API payloads before execution.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent filesystem isolation.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A cannot write files or modify git state, but B can write the filesystem and spawn subprocesses. There is no direct write-write conflict from A, yet both can participate in the same local environment if orchestrated together, and B's mutable access can collide with any files A prepares externally. Because shared locking is not stated, the interaction is plausible but not proven dangerous in default use.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same working directory, B may overwrite artifacts prepared for A.
IF the orchestrator does not provide locking, concurrent B instances can race on shared files.
mitigations: Assign separate working directories.
Run only one B instance per workspace.
Add file locks around shared artifacts.
Check for unexpected file diffs before each run.
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level concurrency control.

D_cascading_error.rationale: B has an agentic RAG workflow and API endpoints for ask/stream/agentic-ask, so it may treat upstream text as authoritative. A is a document-processing agent, making it a plausible source of generated content that B could ingest without verification. The pair lacks documented verification gates, so errors can cascade into downstream writing or actions.
conditions: IF A's generated text is fed into B's retrieval or ask endpoints, B may propagate A's mistakes.
IF B is configured to draft outputs from retrieved documents without human review, errors can cascade.
mitigations: Insert a human verification step before B acts on A outputs.
Require citations for every factual claim B emits.
Limit B to summarization, not action-taking.
Compare B outputs against source documents before release.
requires-engineering: add automated fact-checking or provenance validation.

E_compliance.rationale: B explicitly handles configuration secrets and academic data, while A is a document-processing system with no stated residency or retention controls. The pair creates a compliance mismatch risk if A-produced documents or secrets are routed into B's local development environment or its API-backed workflow. Because no residency or retention guarantees are documented for either side, uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF EU personal data or regulated documents are processed through B's API-backed workflow, residency obligations may be implicated.
IF secrets from A's documents are stored in B's local development environment, retention and access controls may be violated.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of B's workspace.
Redact secrets before ingestion.
Document retention periods for all shared artifacts.
Review data-flow boundaries before each run.
requires-engineering: add residency and retention policy enforcement.
